main_text.p: num in Inimicos, Regem in Subditos decet*
Nil Mihi possunt eripere, quod non libens amittam cum Deo visum fuerit per has manus adimere. Compensabit infinita sua Misericordia, queis nunc humana iniquitate æquum putat me privare.
Decus Mortem sequuturum totum illud exsuperat, quo vel potiri hic poteram, vel cogitare.

Non illas graves amplius & invidiosas hujus Mundi Coronas desiderabo, cum Me Deus misericordia coronaverit, & in Gloria Gratias suas consummaverit, & hanc umbram Terrestrium Regnorum illo vere Cœlesti permutaverit.
Quod ad Mundi probra, & imputatæ Tyrannidis calumnias, ipsa posthac Mei Interemptorum necessaria & acerba sævitia satis omnes per se confutabit.
Horum interim qui optimi & cordatissimi sunt fidem salvam mihi & amorem manere non dubito, quorum multi Me lachrymis & precibus prosequuti sunt, libenter in meam gratiam vel mecum una morituri.

Excusabunt hi facile si qui fuerint lapsus humani, & nihilo minus officium suum ut Regi præstabunt, cum sit nulla tanta a Religione necessitas, quæ sub obtentu puniendi cogat Subditos omnia Principum crimina supe-rare, quæ etiamsi fuisset, hic certe locum non habet, ubi tam prolixa in publicum compensatio facta est, quæque ne publice gauderetur privata Ambitio elusit:

page.notes: The text is set in a single column; the top line is a continuation from the previous page and is cont="true". The running head is printed as ELKΩN BAΣIΛIKH. The Greek is transcribed in Greek capitals as printed. The last line ends with the catchword-like "Cre-" hyphenated word, which is the start of the next word and is kept as printed in the final paragraph's line; it is a line-end hyphenation, not a catchword. Some letters in the scan are faint (notably "illud", "exsuperat" and "compensatio") and were read from context; mark-up such as [?] was not needed for clear words. The phrase "Tyrannidis" and "supe-rare" are split across lines as printed.
